lesson_title: Water Slide Physics: The Race Nobody Wins
hook_text: Steep terrifying slide vs long lazy flume — same height. Who hits the pool faster? Wrong.
clip_script: Two slides empty into the same pool. One is a near-vertical drop that makes queues go quiet. The other is a long, winding, gentle flume. Both start 3,2 metres above the water. Two riders push off from rest at the same moment, one on each. Who hits the pool faster? Neither. Both arrive at exactly 7,92 metres per second. The steep-slide rider arrives SOONER — steep means the trade happens quickly — but not faster. Arrival speed is bought entirely with height, and both riders spent the same 3,2 metres. The slide's shape is just the shop's decor; the price and the purchase are identical. Only the drop counts.
visual_style: Split-screen water park race: steep plunge against winding flume, synced speedometers landing on the same 7,92; overlay of height coins converting to speed coins.
mood: Competitive setup flipped into a delightful anticlimax and an aha.
pacing: Fast race build-up, splash beat, freeze-frame tie reveal, quick ledger explanation, mic-drop close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and solve any roller coaster with one line of energy accounting.
